meta.title: Recording a Song in the Bathtub
meta.textType: story: a conversation about past events

paragraphs: On Monday morning, Teacher Kim listened to a short song on the library tablet. It was the song for the new friends in Singapore. It was one minute long, and it had a picture of the old square on the screen. The sound was clear and warm. "Where did you record it?" she asked. Lily and Mia looked at each other and smiled. Leo and May stood behind them and smiled too.

"At Mia's house, on Saturday afternoon," said Lily. "Leo and May came too, so we were four." "The microphone did not belong to us," said Mia. "A man on our street lent it to us." "He lives three houses away from me." "He is a musician, and he plays the violin." "He said, 'Keep the microphone a little further from your mouth.'"

"Where did you try first?" asked Teacher Kim. "First, we tried the living room," said Leo. "The room was big, and our singing was too loud." "After that, we went to the kitchen." "The fridge made a noise, and you could hear it on the song." "We stopped, and May said, 'This is awful!'" Teacher Kim laughed. "Was it easy?" she asked. "Not at all," said Leo.

"Then we tried the bathroom," said May. "The bathtub was empty and dry, and the walls were close to us." "We sat inside the bathtub with the microphone in the middle." "Our singing sounded big and clear." "Mia's dad closed the door, and the house was quiet." "Lily held the tablet, and Mia counted to three." "We sang the song three times." "At the end, nobody moved for a moment." "The third time was the best," said Mia.

"What is the song about?" asked Teacher Kim. "It is about the dancer in the old town square," said Lily. "Leo wrote the words, and May found the tune." "Mia worked on the tablet for twenty minutes." "She chose the best one and cleaned the sound." "Then I wrote an email to Ms. Ong's class," said Lily. "Grace and Ravi wrote back on Sunday evening." "They liked the song very much."

Teacher Kim gave the tablet back to Lily. "Please thank the musician on your street," she said. "We will give him the microphone back after school," said Mia. "And we will write him a thank-you card."
text.summary: On Monday Teacher Kim asks how the Explorers recorded a song for the pen-pal class. They used a microphone from a neighbor, tried three rooms, and found that an empty bathtub gave the best sound.
